course_summary: This advanced course provides a rigorous, in-depth exposition of computational algorithms, algorithmic complexity, and mathematical optimization across 5 foundational modules: Divide & Conquer Strategies & Recurrences, Dynamic Programming & Greedy Models, Network Flow & Matching, Linear Programming & Approximation Algorithms, and NP-Completeness & Randomized Algorithms. Students develop verifiable competency in formal asymptotic bounds, primal-dual relaxations, poly-time reductions, and randomized derandomization techniques strictly aligned with ABET Engineering Accreditation Criteria.

cos.text: Analyze asymptotic runtime bounds of divide-and-conquer algorithms and recurrent relations using the Akra-Bazzi method and master theorem paradigms.
Design dynamic programming formulations and poly-time reductions for combinatorial optimizations, amortized bounds, and randomized verification.
Implement network flow max-flow min-cut formulations for bipartite matching, circulation with demands, and push-relabel computational constraints.
Formulate linear programming relaxations and dual certificate bounds for vertex cover, set cover, and metric traveling salesperson approximations.
Evaluate complexity class memberships (P, NP, NP-Hard, PSPACE) via formal polynomial-time reductions from 3-SAT, Hamiltonian Cycle, and Subset Sum.
Synthesize randomized algorithms and derandomization techniques (Chernoff bounds, Markov inequality, min-cut Karger contraction) for intractable domains.

co_po_pso_map.rationale: Requires mastery of mathematical induction, Akra-Bazzi integrals, and asymptotic calculus.
Formulates formal recurrence relations and boundary condition constraints.
Designs divide-and-conquer systems for scalable divide-and-conquer computational kernels.
Directly develops rigorous theoretical computer science core competencies.
Applies bellman equation dynamic programming and optimal substructure mathematical proofs.
Analyzes amortized accounting bounds and potential function invariants.
Synthesizes multi-dimensional memoization tables for high-performance combinatorial problems.
Leverages algorithm visualizers and profiling profilers to trace memoized memory cache lines.
Provides foundational algorithmic techniques for state-space search and combinatorial optimization.
Directly transfers to real-world memory-efficient routing and scheduling engines.
Requires deep understanding of graph theory, conservation invariants, and duality bounds.
Proves Max-Flow Min-Cut dual equivalence and capacity cut bottlenecks.
Constructs robust network flow and bipartite matching systems for resource allocation.
Analyzes augmenting path invariants and push-relabel distance labels.
Uses graph visualizers and network flow testbeds.
Essential algorithmic technique for distributed routing and network operations.
Applies to backend request dispatching and microservice load distribution.
Requires matrix algebra, polyhedral geometry, and dual certificate theory.
Formulates constraint optimization and gap analysis.
Designs bounded approximation algorithms for intractable instances.
Leverages modern LP solvers (GLPK, Gurobi) for dual verification.
Underpins advanced computational combinatorial optimization.
Convex optimization is the mathematical engine of neural network training.
Requires mastery of formal language theory and non-deterministic machines.
Establishes formal reduction proofs demonstrating NP-completeness.
Evaluates intractability boundaries and algorithm feasibility limits.
Critical thinking habit for recognizing computationally unsolvable problems.
Distinguishes between polynomial solutions and heuristic approximations.
Requires probability theory, indicator random variables, and tail bounds.
Analyzes expected runtime vs worst-case probability distributions.
Synthesizes randomized data structures (Skip Lists, Bloom Filters).
Employs Monte Carlo simulations to empirically verify convergence.
Core foundation for big data streaming and probabilistic hashing.
Probabilistic modeling aligns directly with modern generative AI architectures.
